meta_description: Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: A working definition of Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric for the enterprise: engineered controls, named owners, weekly evidence, and a signed baseline so every claim of improvement can be replayed line by line.
The problem this solution exists for
Documents sprawl across systems; answers are tribal; permissions inconsistent; freshness SLAs nonexistent — trust dies in month three.
Our approach
We engineer the knowledge estate: corpus inventory and remediation, hybrid retrieval with citations, permission propagation, freshness SLAs, and contribution loops that keep the corpus alive.
Reference architecture

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric
blocks.note: Each stage passes its output forward under a typed contract — schema, owner and freshness agreed in advance; the audit path shares the timeline with the data path.

blocks.x: Every component in Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric has a contract, a version and a named owner. When something drifts, the ticket goes to a person, not to a committee — that is what the reference architecture is for.
Components
Platform stack
Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric runs on platforms you likely already own, composed on contracts rather than replaced by magic — the stack below names each piece and the job it is actually doing.

items: We measure the starting position and lock the baseline with your team — no build work begins before the number is agreed.

Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness

Before Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric starts, three things need to exist: a metric your board recognizes, data access under an approved path, and a named owner on each source system. The readiness check takes two weeks and says no when it should.
How a delivery runs

A delivery for Knowledge & Collaboration Fabric runs on rhythm, not ritual: the baseline is signed in the first weeks, evidence is generated as the work happens, and the gate at each stage has real stop authority. Programs that miss their evidence stop.
Outcomes we commit to

items: time-to-answer is reported against the signed baseline with the evidence attached; if the number stops moving, the program says so.
stale answers is reported with its method note attached, so the delta is reproducible by your analysts, not just ours
knowledge gaps carries the program: if the delta stalls, the gate redirects scope toward it before anything else
